turns.en: I'm just going to take your blood pressure and temperature. Can you roll up your sleeve for me?
turns.cy: Dw i jyst yn mynd i gymryd eich pwysau gwaed chi a'ch tymheredd chi. Fedrwch chi dorchi'ch llawes i mi?
chunks: I'm just going to take your blood pressure and temperature
Dw i jyst yn mynd i gymryd eich pwysau gwaed chi a'ch tymheredd chi
Can you roll up your sleeve for me?
Fedrwch chi dorchi'ch llawes i mi?

turns.en: Of course. Which arm do you want?
turns.cy: Wrth gwrs. Pa fraich dach chi isio?
chunks: pa soft-mutates braich; no do-support in Welsh

turns.en: Left arm's fine. The cuff will squeeze for a few seconds now, then it lets go.
turns.cy: Mae'r fraich chwith yn iawn. Mi fydd y cwff yn gwasgu am chydig eiliadau rŵan — wedyn mae o'n gollwng.
chunks: HG32 verbatim; braich is feminine, so the article mutates it
The cuff will squeeze for a few seconds now
Mi fydd y cwff yn gwasgu am chydig eiliadau rŵan

turns.en: That's not so bad. Tighter than my husband's handshake, mind.
turns.cy: Dydy hynna ddim mor ddrwg. Tynnach nag ysgwyd llaw fy ngŵr i, cofiwch.
chunks: Tynnach nag ysgwyd llaw fy ngŵr i
the synthetic comparative -ach; English's genitive-'s becomes a bare Welsh construct chain
the reminder-tag, an imperative of cofio

turns.en: It's 135 over 80 today - much better. The doctor will be pleased with that.
turns.cy: Mae o'n 135 dros 80 heddiw — llawer gwell. Mi fydd y doctor yn hapus efo hynna.
chunks: HG33 verbatim; the reading is masculine o (R8); read digit-group-wise (R5)
The doctor will be pleased with that
Mi fydd y doctor yn hapus efo hynna

turns.en: 135. I'll remember that - my daughter always asks.
turns.cy: 135. Mi gofia i hynna — mae fy merch i'n gofyn bob tro.
chunks: mae fy merch i'n gofyn bob tro
English's preverbal 'always' lands clause-finally as bob tro

turns.en: I'm just going to check your blood pressure. Roll up your sleeve for me?
turns.cy: Dw i jyst yn mynd i tsiecio'ch pwysau gwaed chi. Torchwch eich llawes i mi?
chunks: I'm just going to check your blood pressure
Dw i jyst yn mynd i tsiecio'ch pwysau gwaed chi
Roll up your sleeve for me?
English's bare request has no Welsh reflex — the -wch imperative under question intonation carries it

turns.en: There we are. It was a bit high yesterday, the other nurse said.
turns.cy: Dyna ni. Roedd o braidd yn uchel ddoe, medda'r nyrs arall.
chunks: It was a bit high yesterday
Roedd o braidd yn uchel ddoe
braidd yn for the hedging 'a bit'
Welsh's quotative medd, not a conjugated verb of saying

turns.en: One high reading on its own is nothing to worry about - that's exactly why we keep checking.
turns.cy: Dydy un darlleniad uchel ar ei ben ei hun ddim byd i boeni amdano fo — dyna'n union pam dan ni'n dal i tsiecio.
chunks: One high reading on its own is nothing to worry about
Dydy un darlleniad uchel ar ei ben ei hun ddim byd i boeni amdano fo
HG35 verbatim; 'on its own' is the ar ei ben ei hun idiom, and 'worry about' conjugates as amdano fo
that's exactly why we keep checking
dyna'n union pam dan ni'n dal i tsiecio

turns.en: So what is it today, then? Is it come down?
turns.cy: Felly be ydy o heddiw, 'ta? Ydy o wedi dod i lawr?
chunks: the in-that-case tag, alongside felly in one sentence — the fork English offers, resolved by role
Ydy o wedi dod i lawr?
the corpus's dialectal perfect maps to the standard Welsh wedi-perfect

turns.en: It's come down nicely - 135 over 80. All done. I'll pop back after lunch to do it again.
turns.cy: Mae o wedi dod i lawr yn ddel — 135 dros 80. Wedi gorffen. Mi bicia i'n ôl ar ôl cinio i'w neud o eto.
chunks: Mae o wedi dod i lawr yn ddel
English's 'all' erases — the bare wedi-perfect carries completion (R3)
I'll pop back after lunch to do it again
Mi bicia i'n ôl ar ôl cinio i'w neud o eto
picio is the northern pop-in verb; the i'w + verbal-noun purpose clause
south: fe bica i / fe alwa i heibio

turns.en: Fat chance of me running off. I'm not going far in these socks.
turns.cy: Does 'na fawr o beryg i mi redeg i ffwrdd. Dw i ddim yn mynd yn bell yn y sanau 'ma.
chunks: Fat chance of me running off
Does 'na fawr o beryg i mi redeg i ffwrdd
English's sarcastic noun phrase relocates to a Welsh negative existential — 'there's little danger of me running off'
I'm not going far in these socks
Dw i ddim yn mynd yn bell yn y sanau 'ma

turns.en: I'm just going to take your blood pressure. Can you roll up your sleeve for me?
turns.cy: Dw i jyst yn mynd i gymryd eich pwysau gwaed chi. Fedrwch chi dorchi'ch llawes i mi?
chunks: I'm just going to take your blood pressure
Dw i jyst yn mynd i gymryd eich pwysau gwaed chi
kept distinct from 'just going to CHECK' → tsiecio — two knowns, two verbs
Can you roll up your sleeve for me?
Fedrwch chi dorchi'ch llawes i mi?

turns.en: You'll have to help me - I can't manage the sleeve with this drip in.
turns.cy: Mi fydd raid i chi fy helpu i — fedra i ddim dod i ben efo'r llawes a'r drip 'ma i mewn.
chunks: Mi fydd raid i chi fy helpu i
English's modal 'have to' relocates to the impersonal bydd raid i frame
fedra i ddim dod i ben efo'r llawes
the walk's one manage-lexeme, dod i ben (cf. 'we'll manage together')

turns.en: Not to worry, we'll use the other arm. Let me just move this table out of your way.
turns.cy: Dim ots — mi wnawn ni ddefnyddio'r fraich arall. Gadwch i mi jyst symud y bwrdd 'ma o'ch ffordd chi.
chunks: HG36 verbatim — English's infinitival has no Welsh reflex; dim ots is the fixed dismissal
mi wnawn ni ddefnyddio'r fraich arall
Let me just move this table out of your way
Gadwch i mi jyst symud y bwrdd 'ma o'ch ffordd chi
gadwch i mi for 'let me' (R3); 'just' outside an imperative keeps jyst

turns.en: Thank you. It's a palaver, this drip. Everywhere I go, it goes.
turns.cy: Diolch. Mae o'n draffarth, y drip 'ma. Lle bynnag dw i'n mynd, mae o'n mynd.
chunks: traffarth is the walk's one bother-lexeme (cf. HG02's trafferth)
Lle bynnag dw i'n mynd, mae o'n mynd

turns.en: It won't be in forever, I promise. There we are - all done for now.
turns.cy: Fydd o ddim i mewn am byth, dw i'n gaddo. Dyna ni — wedi gorffen am rŵan.
chunks: Fydd o ddim i mewn am byth
